{
  "strategy": "increase_nop_bw_to_256",
  "hardware_update": {
    "num_chiplets": 16,
    "compute_units": 16384,
    "buffer_size": 8192,
    "system_params": {"dram_bw": 64, "nop_bw": 256, "micro_batch": 2, "tensor_parall": 16},
    "chiplet_type": "ws"
  },
  "selected_hardware_candidate": "modify_hardware_parameter_1c9c412827b94c25",
  "actions": ["nop_bw: 128->256"],
  "rationale": "The current best configuration (iteration 1) has 16 WS chiplets with 16384 compute units, 64 DRAM BW, 128 NoP BW, tp=16. Bottleneck analysis shows mixed root causes: FFN compute-bound layers (67.6% of time) are already at max compute_units, while memory/communication-bound layers (norm2, res2, res1) define the critical path ending at 19.70s. These layers have 33-54% communication time and 45-66% memory time. Increasing NoP BW from 128 to 256 GB/s directly reduces the communication component of these critical-path layers, which should lower the critical end time and reduce communication energy. The monetary cost of IO is only 12.3% ($29.19), so a bandwidth increase will have a modest cost impact. The compute cost (49.8%) and OS cost (37.9%) remain unchanged. The expected latency reduction from faster NoP communication should compensate for the small IO cost increase, improving the combined objective.",
  "notes": {
    "history_usage": "The only retrieved historical case shows a compute_units increase from 4096 to 16384 improved objective by 54%. No historical cases exist for NoP BW changes, so this is an exploratory move targeting the identified communication bottleneck on the critical path.",
    "cost_risk": "Monetary cost is expected to increase slightly (IO component at 12.3% will grow, but sub-linearly with bandwidth). The latency and energy reductions from faster NoP communication should compensate, as the critical path layers have 33-54% communication time and the timeline shows core5 idle-waiting at 51% utilization.",
    "expected_objective_direction": "decrease",
    "rejected_alternatives": [
      "Increasing DRAM BW from 64 to 128: memory is also a bottleneck (53-66% of critical layers), but DRAM BW increase is more expensive and the communication share is more actionable for NoP. Could be combined in a future iteration.",
      "Increasing compute_units further: already at max (16384).",
      "Increasing num_chiplets to 32: would increase monetary cost significantly (compute + OS costs dominate) and may not help memory/communication-bound layers as much as bandwidth.",
      "Decreasing tensor_parall: would reduce communication but increase per-chiplet compute load, potentially worsening the already compute-bound FFN layers."
    ],
    "risk": "The main risk is that the communication-bound layers are not the dominant latency contributors (only 14.6% of total time vs 67.6% compute). If the critical path is also constrained by DRAM bandwidth, the NoP increase alone may not reduce the critical end time enough to justify the IO cost increase. However, the timeline shows core5 idle-waiting at 10.12s busy vs 19.70s critical end, suggesting data movement is the limiter."
  }
}
